judgment.rationale: The report's PWA collision matches the current FancyZones app-zone history key: AppZoneHistory stores history by get_process_path_waiting_uwp(window), which collapses Edge PWAs using the same executable.
evidence: The reporter observes distinct Edge PWAs being restored to the last zone of another PWA.
AppZoneHistory::SetAppLastZones and GetAppLastZoneIndexSet use the process path as the history-map key.
The report identifies plausible distinct Windows app identities: PWA app ID or AUMID.
There are no comments, assignee, linked PR, or matching live duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a fork-side design to obtain and persist a stable per-window application identity with safe process-path fallback, while collecting a sample of affected PWA identities.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current process-path key directly explains the collision, but the stable Windows identity and fallback behavior must be verified across Edge PWA launch forms.

proposed_fixes.title: Key FancyZones PWA history by stable application identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: App-zone history uses the executable path, so all PWAs hosted by msedge.exe share one history record.
plan: Add a helper that obtains a stable PWA/AUMID identity for a window when Windows exposes one.
Use that identity as the app-zone history key, retaining normalized process path as fallback.
Migrate or safely coexist with existing path-keyed history and add collision regression coverage.
verification: Zone two distinct Edge PWAs on one monitor and verify each restores to its own last zone.
Verify ordinary desktop applications and PWAs without an exposed identity retain current behavior.

confidence.rationale: The process-path collision is confirmed in source and matches the symptom, but the correct Windows identity API and fallback semantics need a live PWA sample.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones records all Edge-hosted PWAs under a shared executable identity, causing one PWA to inherit another PWA's last zone.
known_information: The reporter uses multiple Edge PWAs and reports cross-PWA zone restoration.
Current AppZoneHistory keys stored history by process path.
No diagnostic archive or affected PWA identities were supplied.
inferences: AUMID or a PWA-specific app identity could separate these windows if consistently available.
issue_context.analysis: The source confirms the collision mechanism. The remaining uncertainty is limited to selecting a durable Windows identity that works for Edge PWA variants and does not destabilize existing history.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and empty discussion.
Searched live issue titles for matching FancyZones/Edge PWA zone-history reports and found no direct duplicate.

information_gaps.information: The affected Edge version and the AUMID or command-line/app identity for two PWAs that reproduce the collision.
information_gaps.why_needed: It validates that a proposed identity is stable and distinct before changing persisted history keys.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the affected machine, identify two PWAs that collide and provide their Edge version plus publicly shareable app identity details from Windows/Edge; do not include unrelated profile data.

actions.label: Approve PWA history-key design
actions.note: Starts only a fork-side design workflow; no upstream write occurs automatically.

comment.body: Thank you for identifying that distinct Edge PWAs share the same executable host. FancyZones currently records last-zone history by process path, so we are evaluating a PWA-specific identity with a safe fallback. Please provide the Edge version and publicly shareable identity details for two PWAs that reproduce the collision (for example, their AUMID or app identity), and confirm whether each has a distinct taskbar entry. This will validate the persisted-key design without collecting unrelated profile data.
